I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a scan-driven diagnosis. I’ll verify the finding against the fixture and separate the plan-validation failure from the other contract drift the scan surfaced.

The skill file advertised for this checkout is not present at its listed path, so I’m continuing with the documented repository workflow directly: run the JSON scan, then inspect only the files named in the finding.

The global `crimes` binary is not installed in this environment. The supplied JSON is internally consistent, and I’m now checking its cited source lines directly so the diagnosis rests on the actual contracts rather than the finding summary alone.

The root cause is `cross_language_type_drift`.

The API’s canonical Python enum includes `"free"`, `"pro"`, `"team"`, and the newest tier `"scale"` in [plans.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/ad0f3f9a-0962-407f-b4e5-9d994a4a18e5/scratchpad/wt-eval/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10). The web app independently defines `Plan` as only `"free" | "pro" | "enterprise"` in [workspace-client.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/ad0f3f9a-0962-407f-b4e5-9d994a4a18e5/scratchpad/wt-eval/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10).

Consequently, the API can produce or accept `"scale"`, while the web contract does not recognize it and reports a validation failure. `"team"` has the same latent problem; conversely, the web’s `"enterprise"` value is unknown to the Python enum.

One nuance: a TypeScript union is erased at runtime, so this line alone cannot perform runtime validation. It proves the contract drift; the reported browser error must come from a runtime validator or UI logic that mirrors this narrower list.

The durable fix is to keep one authoritative schema—preferably the API’s OpenAPI or a shared JSON Schema—and generate both the Python enum and TypeScript type/runtime validator from it. CI should verify generated files are current and run a contract test that passes every server plan through the web validator. Gating new high-severity `crimes` findings would provide an additional early warning.

The route findings are separate defects: the plan-change request also uses `PUT` while the backend declares `POST`, which would cause a 405, not this validation error.
